solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: B paraphrases the final paragraph's 'weather often determines when', which also cues R013-02 and R013-07 (weather as timing cue)
R013-01.notes: Final paragraph: division of labor among stored resources, weather (when), predator satiation and pollination. A contradicts 'weather does affect seed production'; C is one part only; D is the rejected older view.

flags: minor: D is the longest choice and nearly copies paragraph 5 ('cue', 'stored resources', 'not ... the reason'); answer also cued by R013-01 B
R013-02.notes: Para 5 recasts weather as a regional cue to commit stored resources, 'not, by itself, the reason they produce so many seeds.' A overstates rejection; B is the paragraph-1 view; C has no support.

R013-03.notes: Para 2 concludes 'Whatever coordinates them, it seems to be more than the weather each tree happens to experience.' B contradicts 'Weather does affect seed production'; C/D unsupported.

R013-04.notes: Masting most pronounced where seeds eaten by specialists, so least pronounced with generalists (C). A, B, D all describe dependent/specialist eaters. LEAST reversal is the small twist; B is the likeliest trap but its population tracking the crop marks it as dependent.

flags: minor: D 'predicted' is a proximity trap since 'predicts' appears in the same sentence; fine as a distractor
R013-05.notes: 'Most pronounced' = most marked/conspicuous. Spoken and declared are the common senses; standard vocabulary-in-context item.

flags: minor: A's rationale ('little of the pollen in the air would reach its flowers') is a slight inference beyond the text's 'would waste much of the effort', but clearly supported
R013-06.notes: Para 4 last sentence states such a tree 'would waste much of the effort.' A reuses that wording; C reverses; B and D unsupported.

flags: minor: A and D are exact mirror reversals, so test-wise students narrow to two quickly
R013-07.notes: Paras 3-4 give benefits (predator satiation, pollination efficiency); para 5 opens 'Neither explanation tells us how trees ... manage to act together' and supplies the weather cue. A swaps them; B and C unsupported.

R013-08.notes: 'An arrangement that no single tree designed, but one that the forest, over many generations, has come to depend on' = shared pattern that developed without a plan. A contradicts 'no single tree designed'; B overreads 'depend on'; D not a new hypothesis.

R013-09.notes: Para 1: treated as a matter of weather (warm spring/wet summer large crop; frost/drought small). B, C, D are later alternative explanations, not the twentieth-century view.
